title: The History of Assassin's Creed | From 2007 to Black Flag Resynced | Gaming History
description: The full history of Assassin's Creed: the Prince of Persia origin, the Ezio trilogy, Black Flag, the shift to role playing with Origins, Mirage, Shadows in Japan and the Black Flag Resynced remake in July twenty twenty six.

sections.heading: The creed that conquered history
sections.script: Hidden blades, rooftop chases and a leap of faith into a pile of hay. Assassin's Creed has taken players from the Third Crusade to ancient Egypt, from Viking England to feudal Japan. It is Ubisoft's best selling franchise, and in July of twenty twenty six the publisher said it had passed two hundred and fifty million copies sold worldwide. In this video we walk through the history of Assassin's Creed, game by game. We start with an idea that began life as a Prince of Persia spin off, follow the Ezio trilogy and the pirate adventure of Black Flag, see how the series reinvented itself as a role playing game, and finish with Shadows and the brand new Black Flag Resynced remake. Grab your hidden blade, because this is a long journey.

sections.heading: From Prince of Persia to Assassin's Creed
sections.script: The story starts with Patrice Desilets, who had been creative director on Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time. He did not want to make another game about a prince, so he pitched a concept built around the bodyguards and killers who surround a ruler, under the working title Prince of Persia: Assassins. The idea grew into something much bigger, and the prince was dropped. Jade Raymond joined as producer, and the project became a brand new franchise. Assassin's Creed launched in November of two thousand seven on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, with a Windows version following in April of two thousand eight. You played Desmond Miles, who relived the memories of his ancestor Altair through a machine called the Animus. Reviews were generally favorable, and Ubisoft reported eight million copies sold by April of two thousand nine.

sections.heading: The Ezio trilogy
sections.script: If the first game was the proof of concept, the second was the breakthrough. Assassin's Creed Two arrived in two thousand nine and moved the action to Renaissance Italy, introducing Ezio Auditore da Firenze, a young nobleman who becomes an assassin. Fans loved his story, the beautiful cities of Florence and Venice, and the freedom to climb almost anything. Ubisoft followed it with Assassin's Creed Brotherhood in two thousand ten, set in Rome, and Assassin's Creed Revelations in two thousand eleven, set in Constantinople. Together they follow Ezio from his teenage years to old age, and many players still call this trilogy the heart of the series. Three games, one hero, and a story that many fans still remember fondly.

sections.heading: Revolution and the pirate years
sections.script: Assassin's Creed Three came out in two thousand twelve and took the series to the American colonies during the Revolutionary era, with the new hero Connor. Then came a huge surprise. Assassin's Creed Four: Black Flag launched on October twenty ninth, twenty thirteen, and it turned the series into a pirate adventure. You played Edward Kenway, a Welsh privateer turned pirate, and you captained your own brig, the Jackdaw. Sailing between islands, fighting naval battles and boarding enemy ships without loading screens was a major focus of the game, and critics praised it. The story is set in the Caribbean during the Golden Age of Piracy, with cities such as Havana, Nassau and Kingston. For many fans, Black Flag remains the favorite game in the whole series.

sections.heading: Unity, Rogue and Syndicate
sections.script: In two thousand fourteen, Ubisoft released two games. Assassin's Creed Unity took players to Paris during the French Revolution, with Arno Dorian as the hero,. Assassin's Creed Rogue, on the other hand, followed Shay Cormac, an assassin who turns against his own brotherhood. In two thousand fifteen came Assassin's Creed Syndicate, which launched on October twenty third on consoles and arrived on Windows in November. It is set in Victorian London and stars the twin assassins Jacob and Evie Frye. After Syndicate, Ubisoft decided the series needed a rest. There was no new main game in two thousand sixteen. The only Assassin's Creed release that year was a live action film, starring Michael Fassbender, which reached the United States on December twenty first and earned about two hundred and forty one million dollars worldwide.

sections.heading: Origins and the RPG revolution
sections.script: The break paid off. Assassin's Creed Origins launched on October twenty seventh, twenty seventeen, for PlayStation 4, Xbox One and Windows, and it changed the formula. Earlier games were mainly stealth action adventures. Origins added levels, experience points, a skill tree and a combat system based on hitboxes, so it felt much more like a role playing game. You played Bayek, a Medjay from Siwa, in Egypt during the time of Cleopatra around forty nine B C. His story leads to the founding of the Hidden Ones, the forerunners of the Assassin Brotherhood. The game also introduced Discovery Tour, a free mode with no combat that offers guided tours of ancient Egypt. It arrived in February of twenty eighteen, and teachers and history lovers welcomed it.

sections.heading: Odyssey and Valhalla
sections.script: Ubisoft kept going with the role playing formula. Assassin's Creed Odyssey arrived in twenty eighteen and moved to classical Greece in the year four thirty one B C, letting you choose between two heroes, Alexios or Kassandra. Then came Assassin's Creed Valhalla in twenty twenty, set in Viking age England and Norway in the years from eight seventy two, with Eivor as the main character. Valhalla's launch was strong, and Ubisoft later said it had the biggest day one sales of any game in the franchise. Together, Origins, Odyssey and Valhalla form what fans call the role playing trilogy. They are huge open worlds with long stories, plenty of side quests and endless things to discover, and they brought millions of new players to the series.

sections.heading: Mirage goes back to the roots
sections.script: Not everyone wanted a giant role playing game, so in two thousand twenty three Ubisoft released something smaller. Assassin's Creed Mirage came out on October fifth, twenty twenty three. It is set in Baghdad in the year eight sixty one, and it stars Basim, who players met in Valhalla. Ubisoft aimed for a return to the classic style, with a focus on stealth, parkour and a more compact city, rather than a giant map. It was a prequel to Valhalla, and it showed that the series could still tell a more focused story. The same year also brought Assassin's Creed Nexus VR, a spin off for Meta Quest headsets. Mirage was a short and sweet reminder of where the series began.

sections.heading: Shadows arrives in Japan
sections.script: For years, fans asked for one thing: feudal Japan. Assassin's Creed Shadows delivered it. After being delayed twice, first from November of twenty twenty four to February and then to March, it finally launched on March twentieth, twenty twenty five, on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, Windows and Mac. A version for Nintendo Switch Two followed on December second. The story is set in the Sengoku period from fifteen seventy nine, and you switch between two heroes: Naoe, a shinobi, and Yasuke, a samurai inspired by a real historical figure. Ubisoft said that the game passed one million players on launch day and three million within a week. It later reported more than five million players, though that count includes subscription services as well as sales.

sections.heading: Black Flag comes back
sections.script: Fans had begged for a Black Flag remake for years, and in twenty twenty six it finally happened. Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced launched on July ninth, twenty twenty six, for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and Windows. It brings improved visuals, a dynamic weather system, more officers to recruit and new side quests, while leaving out the original modern day storyline and the multiplayer mode. Ubisoft said that it sold two million copies on its first day and more than three million in its first week. Critics were positive, with a Metacritic score of eighty four according to Ubisoft. Alongside the launch, Vantage Studios announced that the whole franchise had passed two hundred and fifty million copies sold. Not bad for a series that began as a Prince of Persia idea.

sections.heading: Which Assassin's Creed is your favorite
sections.script: From a hidden blade in the Holy Land to a ship's wheel in the Caribbean and a shinobi in Japan, Assassin's Creed has changed again and again while keeping its spirit of history, secrets and freedom. Fourteen main games, a movie, and more than two hundred and fifty million copies sold show how far it has come. So now it is your turn. Which Assassin's Creed is your favorite, the Ezio trilogy, Black Flag, Origins, or the newest, Shadows? And which setting do you want next? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history of Assassin's Creed, subscribe for more gaming history videos, like the video, and we will see you in the next one.
